clue.text: Leave suddenly, as banks of Dee affected

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so take the outside letters of the word Dee

parts.note: affected, as in showy and mannered, means camp

explanation.surface: Someone flees in a hurry as the River Dee bursts its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks of' takes the outer letters of Dee, giving DE. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart abruptly, often secretly, as soldiers striking camp.

clue.text: Reserved reduced object

indicators.note: reduced says the word for reserved loses its last letter

parts.note: reserved means demure, modest and quiet

explanation.surface: A shy person has been cut down to a mere thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the E off DEMURE; 'object' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise objections or show reluctance.

clue.text: Opener in county's team

parts.note: Cork is an Irish county; with the 's it gives Cork's
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A batsman who opens the innings for a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket opening batsman; it is a bottle opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is a tool that opens wine bottles.

clue.text: Cross about new flirtatious girl

indicators.note: about says the mixing word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to cross breeds is to mix them

explanation.surface: An angry remark about a new coquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but means MIX, which goes about N.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky or flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Injury caused by a couple of cats

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
a cat is also a lash, the scourge used for flogging

explanation.surface: Someone has been hurt in a scrap with two felines.
explanation.walkthrough: The cats are not animals but the cat-o'-nine-tails; two synonyms for it sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck injury from a sudden jolt, typically in a car crash, is known by this name.

clue.text: Frequent visitor somewhat put in the shade

indicators.note: put in says the phrase for somewhat goes inside the colour word

parts.note: a shade is a hue
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: A regular customer is rather overshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests darkness, but is a colour: A BIT goes in HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular at a place such as a bar or club.

clue.text: Criticise judge as well as odd pompous official

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
as well as means and
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Attacking a judge and a strange self-important bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A panjandrum is a self-important person in authority.

clue.text: Useful thing, when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived
fixed means set

explanation.surface: Something becomes handy once it has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable resource or advantage.

clue.text: Gyrating dancer in hot bar

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: gyrating means whirling, so the letters of dancer and in are spun about

explanation.surface: A dancer spinning in a steamy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gyrating' rearranges DANCER plus IN into INDRANCE, after H; 'bar' is an obstacle, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar in the sense of an obstacle is a hindrance.

clue.text: Start to speak about black fish

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Raising the subject of a dark-coloured fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion.

clue.text: Sailor in unpleasant rain in sea off Calais?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the French sea word

parts.note: Calais is in France, where the sea is la mer

indicators.note: unpleasant suggests the word rain is turned into a nasty jumble

explanation.surface: A seafarer is caught in a downpour in the Channel off the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpleasant' rearranges RAIN into ARIN, which goes inside MER, French for sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariner is an old or literary synonym for a seaman.

clue.text: Blessing given by one disciple on mountain

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
one is the Roman numeral I
son can mean a disciple or follower, as in the sons of the prophets

explanation.surface: A blessing is bestowed by one of the apostles on a mount, like the Sermon on the Mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' here means placed after: I and SON follow BEN in the across light.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an archaic or literary word for a spoken benediction.

clue.text: Reckless prang, not chauffeur's first

indicators.note: not says the chosen letter is dropped from the crash word

parts.note: prang is British slang for a car crash

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of chauffeur's

explanation.surface: A careless driver's bump, though the chauffeur wasn't to blame first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C, the first letter of 'chauffeur's', from CRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without thought of consequences, a synonym of reckless.

clue.text: Expert old academic, endlessly severe

parts.note: something old is past
an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for severe is cut off

parts.note: severe means stern

explanation.surface: A veteran scholar who is skilled but unrelentingly strict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is someone thoroughly skilled in an activity, a seasoned expert.

clue.text: Extraordinarily rare opportunity to see a Hitchcock film

indicators.note: extraordinarily signals the letters of rare are set out of their ordinary order

parts.note: a window is an opportunity, as in a window of time

explanation.surface: A rare chance to see a classic thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' rearranges RARE into REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear Window is the 1954 Alfred Hitchcock thriller.

clue.text: Charm of Arab, say, at Oxford?

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, an example signalled by say
an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A good-luck token belonging to an Arab student at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the university town but a kind of shoe; 'of' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck talisman.

clue.text: What's bound to put an end to children's game?

parts.note: a bound is a hop, and the 's gives hop's
to scotch is to put an end to a plan or rumour

explanation.surface: Asking what will stop children from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'tied' or 'certain', but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Culvert dry? Originally, before wet weather

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word dry

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Asking whether a channel is empty before the downpour arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first letter of 'dry', goes before RAIN; 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A culvert is a channel or pipe carrying water, much like a drain.

clue.text: Plant a girl put on shelf knocked over

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

indicators.note: knocked over says the shelf word is overturned, read upwards

parts.note: a sill is a shelf, as on a window

explanation.surface: A girl sets a pot plant on a shelf and it falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns SILL to LLIS; 'put on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a bulb plant with large trumpet flowers.

clue.text: Energy authority

definitions.meaning: energy as in electricity or force
authority as in control or command over others

explanation.definitionFit: Power covers both physical energy and the right to command.

clue.text: Please cut out conjecture

indicators.note: out signals these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A request to remove some guesswork from a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal for PLEASECUT; 'conjecture' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjecture is to guess or form a theory without proof, the same as to theorise idly.

clue.text: Having indefinite number, note, aboard, lifeboatman's capsized in river

indicators.note: aboard puts the two letters on board the overturned name
capsized says the boatman's name is turned upside down, read upwards in this down light

parts.note: Noah built the ark, a lifeboat of sorts, hence Noah's
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: A sailor's boat overturns in a river, with an unknown number of people on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns NOAHS into SHAON; N and N go 'aboard'. The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is a major river in Ireland.

clue.text: Oddly silent recruit

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters of silent arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A quiet new army member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but here it is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join up or sign on, as a recruit does.

clue.text: Big-hearted cleaner, albeit scatty

explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British cleaning woman; 'scatty' turns ALBEIT into ITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A big-hearted person is generous and kind, the same as a giving one.

clue.text: Beginning to ascend with energy, energy in abundance

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of ascend

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
go again means energy

explanation.surface: Starting to climb with lots and lots of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore and a-gogo both mean plentifully, in large numbers.

clue.text: Song suggested by that man on the radio

parts.note: that man as an object pronoun is him

explanation.surface: A tune requested by a particular listener on air.
explanation.walkthrough: HIM and HYMN sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise.

clue.text: Head of Hermes displayed in pleasant corner

parts.note: pleasant means nice

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of Hermes

explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is a link; H goes in NICE.

clue.text: Lover's knot, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied with loops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover's knot' looks like one phrase; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Crushed hot rod, dented in part

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A customised car has been crushed and dented in places.

clue.text: Rings back about the man's record
